title: Is Jordy Frahm putting Nebraska softball on the map?
text:
Nebraska softball has made a comeback within the last five or six years. Just a few years ago, they were having a split season back in 2022. However, in the most recent season, the Huskers only lost eight of their 60 games, tying their all-time win record. What caused this change in the team? Could it be the star transfer from Oklahoma?


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

nebraska <- read_csv("~/Documents/SPMC 350/Blog/posts/jordy-frahm-putting-nebraska-on-the-map/Nebraska games.csv")

nebraskalong <- nebraska |> 
  pivot_longer( 
  cols = 3:4, 
    names_to = "outcome_type", 
    values_to = "games"
    )

ggplot() +
  geom_bar(
    data = nebraskalong, 
    aes(
      x = Season,
      weight = games,
      fill = outcome_type
    )
  ) + 
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("#E41C38", "black"),
    name="Outcome",
    labels = c("Losses", "Wins"
    )
  ) + 
  labs(
    x="", 
    y="Total games", 
    title="Oklahoma transfer changed trajectory of Nebraska",
    subtitle="Jordy Frahm's transfer in 2024 contributed to rise in success from Husker softball for her remaining two years.", 
    caption="Source: Nebraska Softball | By Jaci Swain" 
    ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 









Jordy Frahm transferred to Nebraska in her third year in college, and it has been game-changing. Although following the transfer, she sustained an injury in the first game of the season in 2024 against the University of Washington. Once she bounced back in the 2025 season, she has not taken her foot off the gas pedal, and neither has the rest of the team. Overall, in her total college career, she holds the highest batting average of .430, going 157-365.
Her pitching has been great over her time at Nebraska. Frahm also holds the fourth record for win percentage in Husker history with .758, having a total of 47 wins. As well as holding the ninth record for earned run average with 1.51 over her entire career and being top 10 in strikeouts.
During her time at Nebraska, Frahm holds the records for multiple different all-time Husker career records, including a tie in complete game no-hitters, tying with Rhonda Revelle and Hannah Camenzind. Frahm currently holds the second record for saves with 14, two less than the all-time record of 16 held by Lori Sippel.


Code
hitting <- read_csv("~/Documents/SPMC 350/Blog/posts/jordy-frahm-putting-nebraska-on-the-map/Individual hitting stats 2026.csv")

pitching <- read_csv("~/Documents/SPMC 350/Blog/Posts/jordy-frahm-putting-nebraska-on-the-map/Nebraska pitching 2026 ind.csv")

newhitting <- hitting |> 
  filter(
    AVG > 0.000
    ) |> 
  top_n(5, wt = AVG)

jfh <- newhitting |> filter(Player == "Jordy Frahm")

hch <- newhitting |> filter(Player == "Hannah Camenzind")

bar1 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(
    data= newhitting,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        AVG),
      weight=AVG),
    fill= "lightgrey") +
  geom_bar(
    data= jfh,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        AVG),
      weight=AVG),
    fill= "#E41C38") +
   labs(
    x="", 
    y="Batting Average"
    ) + geom_bar(
    data= hch,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        AVG),
      weight=AVG),
    fill= "darkgrey") +
   labs(
    x="", 
    y="Batting Average"
    ) + 
  coord_flip()

jfp <- pitching |> filter(Player == "Jordy Frahm")

hcp <- pitching |> filter(Player == "Hannah Camenzind")

bar2<- ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(
    data= pitching,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        SO),
      weight= SO), 
    fill= "lightgrey") +
   geom_bar(
    data= jfp,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        SO),
      weight= SO),
    fill= "#E41C38") +
   labs(
    x="", 
    y="Earned Run Average"
    ) +
  geom_bar(
    data= hcp,
    aes(
      x=reorder(
        Player,
        SO),
      weight= SO),
    fill= "darkgrey") +
   labs(
    x="", 
    y="Pitching Strikeouts"
    ) +
  coord_flip()

bar1 + bar2 + 
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Jordy Frahm dominating Nebraska",
    subtitle = "A comparison of the Husker's 2026 batting averages and pitching strikeouts.",
    caption = "Source: Nebraska Softball | By Jaci Swain"
  ) & 
  theme +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) 









Just in 2026, she had an average of .403 for hitting, and led the team in strikeouts for pitching. During her final season, Frahm finished with 20 home runs, three ahead of the next player. She has been an unstoppable force, along with the rest of her team. Only two pitchers are double-dipping into hitting. Hanah Camenzind, while not producing many strikeouts, is third on the team in batting average.
With all the success comes fans, right? Well, that would be the case here as well. The Cornhuskers have been playing in front of a much larger crowd over the last two years. After Frahm’s transfer, there has been an undeniable increase in audience for home games. This includes 2026, when they did not play in front of a crowd of less than 2,000. The work they have been putting in is being seen by fans as well.
This is a team sport after all, but who’s to say that her success this past season did not have a major impact on the team? After her final season, Frahm became an assistant coach for the Huskers. Where does this leave the future of Nebraska softball?


Code
crowd <- read_csv("~/Documents/SPMC 350/Homework/Project Data/Nebraska home crowds.csv")

Season2024 <- crowd |> filter(Season == 2024)

Season2025 <- crowd |> filter(Season == 2025)

Season2026 <- crowd |> filter(Season == 2026)

 ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data=crowd, aes(x=Date, y=attendance, group=Season)) + 
   geom_line(data=Season2024, aes(x=Date, y=attendance, group=Season), color = "#E41C38") + 
   geom_line(data=Season2025, aes(x=Date, y=attendance, group=Season), color = "#E41C38") + 
   geom_line(data=Season2026, aes(x=Date, y=attendance, group=Season), color = "#E41C38") + 
    facet_grid(~ Season) + 
  labs(
    x="Attendance", 
    y="", 
    title="Crowds shuffling into Bowling Stadium",
    subtitle="Nebrabaska attendance has risen within the last five years, with no game hosting less than a thousand people.", 
    caption="Source: Nebraska Softball | By Jaci Swain" 
    ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )
